slides.title: Chicago Bears Question of the Day: Will injuries in the secondary derail the season?
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>n I’ve been trying to argue on behalf of the Chicago Bears’ secondary for three seasons now. There is just too much talent to ignore. This year, Jaylon Johnson, Kyler Gordon, Coby Bryant, Dillon Thieneman, Tyrique Stevenson, Malik Muhammad, Terrell Smith, and Cam Lewis are a formidable group. Throw in the likes of past Bears Kevin Byard, Jaquan Brisker, Nashon Wright, and more and the Bears have been swarming in talent over the last few years.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) Despite leading the league in takeaways last season, it still felt like the secondary over the last few seasons has been underperforming. A lot of that is due to persisting injuries to important talents. The 2026 offseason has not been kind to this unit so far, either.

slides.title: OC Matt Nagy: Giants only ‘halfway through’ installing their offense
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>More often than not throughout the early stages of New York Giants training camp, the defense has gotten the better of the offense during team periods. That is cause for alarm among some on the fan base . There are many who did not like the hiring of Matt Nagy as offensive coordinator, and aren’t sure how the Giants’ offense is going to come together with multiple former head coaches or play callers on the staff.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) Nagy offered a hint regarding why the offense has not been better during first first media availability of training camp on Tuesday. As Nagy explains it, the offense we are seeing is far from complete, and far from polished. “We’re halfway through camp right now. We have still two and a half weeks. We’re halfway through our run install and halfway through our pass install, if it gives you any perspective,” Nagy said.

slides.title: The Science of “Ramping Up”: Why Aaron Glenn Playing Starters is a Calculated Risk Worth Taking
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>For years, the conventional wisdom in NFL training camps was simple: wrap the starters in bubble wrap, hold them out of preseason games, save them for Week 1. And every September, like clockwork, the league watches soft-tissue injuries pile up anyway – hamstrings, calves, Achilles, all the non contact stuff that has nothing to do with getting hit and everything to do with a body that wasn’t ready to go full speed. There’s actually a real world test of this. In 2020,

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) the NFL canceled the entire preseason because of COVID. No joint practices, no exhibition games, nothing. Researchers compared that season’s regular season injury numbers to 2018-19 and found soft-tissue injuries jumped hard.

slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>Fall camp is always the gumpiest time of year, as optimism abounds. Jah-Marien Latham, Alabama’s longest-tenured player, stood out during this drill. The wolves also did some one-on-one swim moves against each other, which defensive coordiantor Kane Wommack was right there for.

slides.title: Drake Maye not worried about making Patriots receivers happy: ‘My job is to score points’
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>Foxborough, MA - July 28: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and wide receiver Mack Hollins shake hands at training camp on July 28, 2026. Looking at this year’s training camp, the team appears to have succeeded. In his third summer, Drake Maye gets to work with a top-tier running back duo, an intriguing group of tight ends, and a wide receiver room that currently stands at seven roster-worthy players deep. Of course,

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) the numbers create some problems that very well can be placed into the “first world” category: how do you keep all of the receiving talent involved and happy?For Maye, the answer is simple. You don’t, at least not by trying to spread the wealth in a traditional sense. “I think the best thing for that is winning,” he explained following Tuesday’s joint practice with the Indianapolis Colts. “Nobody really tries to complain when you win games.

"If I do, great. If not,

slides.title: Jets announce Qwan’tez Stiggers has been released from the hospital
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>When Jets cornerback Qwan’tez Stiggers was taken off the practice field on a stretcher Tuesday, it was a scary moment. But it appears that Stiggers is going to be fine. The Jets have announced that Stiggers was released from the hospital and is home recovering. Stiggers ended up needing to be in the hospital for only a few hours after passing out on the sideline during practice.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) It's unclear what led him to pass out and there's been no word on when he might be back at practice. The 24-year-old Stiggers is heading into his third season with the Jets. He's an easy player to root for given his journey to the NFL after never playing college football. Stiggers went from high school football to the Fan Controlled Football league and then signed with the Toronto Argonauts of the Canadian Football League.

slides.title: Ranking MLB teams by World Series titles: Which clubs have never won?
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>Every February, all 30 MLB franchises begin spring training with a renewed sense of hope. Their bodies are rested, their eyes already on the fall with the dream of hoisting the Commissioner's Trophy as World Series champions. It's an exclusive club . . . but not as exclusive as you might expect. All in all, 25 out of 30 big league franchises have won at least one championship. Out of the five who have yet to win one, <<<INDENT>>>(cont) only the Seattle Mariners have yet to appear in a World Series.

slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>ST. Paul, Minnesota. John’s, and, of course, Villanova — announced that it had hired Tim Brosnan as its new commissioner. slides.title: Cal Raleigh gives blunt assessment of his performance with Mariners mired in losing streak: 'I'm awful'
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>One could argue Cal Raleigh was the story of the 2025 MLB season. Sure, Aaron Judge walked away with the American League MVP, but Raleigh was the breakout superstar. He clubbed 60 home runs, made his first All-Star team and won the Home Run Derby. A year later, though, Raleigh is literally one of the worst hitters in the game. With the Mariners quickly falling out of the playoff hunt after losing their fifth-straight game, <<<INDENT>>>(cont) Raleigh surprised reporters by inviting an impromptu Q&A after Tuesday’s 4-1 loss to the New York Yankees.

slides.title: Tigers seek series-clinching win over Guardians on Wednesday night
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>The Detroit Tigers took the first game of a critical home series against the Cleveland Guardians on Tuesday night with a narrow 6-4 victory. The good guys got their first win against Tanner Bibee since July 2024 thanks to some well-timed offense, and somehow, Kenley Jansen did not blow the save despite feeding the batters meatballs in the ninth. Taking the mound for the Motor City Kitties in Game 2 is left-hander Framber Valdez, who is coming off two straight seven-

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) inning quality starts. Across those 14 frames of work, the 32-year-old veteran posted a 1.29 ERA and 2.38 FIP on 14 hits and four walks — good for a 1.29 WHIP — while striking out 11 en route to a pair of wins. Valdez faced Cleveland once before this season on May 18 in Detroit, and it was not pretty, serving up four runs on five hits and four walks while striking out three over five innings of work to take the L in an 8-2 loss.

slides.title: Orioles news: Alonso, Henderson power O’s to big win
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>For whatever reason, the O’s bats are able to provide run support when Young is on the mound, and they did so again on Tuesday night. Three home runs in the first three innings gave the O’s an early 5-2 lead, and that is exactly where the score would remain for the rest of the game. Scoring five times in three innings is good! Getting shut out for the final six innings is bad. That is the 2026 Orioles experience in a nutshell. But on this night, <<<INDENT>>>(cont) it was good enough for the win.

slides.title: Could Tarik Skubal go home to Tigers? What history says about MLB rental stars
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>There's a version of this story that ends with Tarik Skubal back in Detroit, embraced by Tigers fans. It's just not the one that anybody in the Motor City is hoping for. Skubal has been a Los Angles Dodger for a little over a week and he hasn't stopped talking about the team that traded him. "I would love to play my whole career in Detroit," he said on Pardon My Take, adding that he hopes talks pick back up in November once the playoff are over.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) Tigers fans heard hope in that sentence. The rest of the league heard a well-prepared, soon-to-be free agent represented by Scott Boras looking to keep his market open as wide as possible. All bidders are welcome.

slides.title: Which hitter could be cut following possible star returns?
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>It’s a tough time to do so, as players around the league certainly get gassed by the dog days of summer as the grind of the 162-game season really sets in. The Yanks got a 4-1 win over the Mariners last night, but it’s an unflattering statement on the offense when four runs—in one inning, no less!—feels like an explosion for this team. They must press on regardless and hope that some slumping bats awaken while the pitching remains elite.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) The Yankees obviously hope to get all of Judge, Stanton, and Bellinger back at various points over the next month and change; manager Aaron Boone suggested that the reverse order could be most likely. Outside of Bellinger, their injuries have been fuzzy enough that I’m not going to personally focus on their returns until they’re actually in the lineup. But I do think that at absolute minimum, Bellinger will be back and Judge will appear in a lineup again by season’s end.

slides.title: Yankees news: Giancarlo Stanton runs bases as rehab continues
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>Steinbrenner Field. n New York Daily News Gary Phillips: At this point in the 2026 season, Giancarlo Stanton has been out so long that he almost feels like an afterthought, as he last played on April 24th in Houston. The calf injury was said to be minor, but sadly nothing truly is with MLB’s active home run leader. If nothing else, Stanton at least hit a milestone in the rehab process yesterday, participating in on-

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) field baserunning drills at Yankee Stadium for the first time since June (when his calf strain recurred). He had been working on his hitting, but he hadn’t previously done this during the process. Stanton has avoided rehab appearances in recent years since as a DH, the Trajekt pitching machines do an excellent job of replicating game action.

slides.title: Sugano Continues to Have the Dbacks Number: Dbacks 2, Rockies 3
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>If you would’ve asked most Dbacks fans at this point, they would probably be feeling pretty good about the rest of the game considering what this team has done to the Rockies this season. However, Sugano had different thoughts. All in all the young lefty Mitch Bratt looked pretty good tonight as he allowed just the 2 run home run over 6 innings tonight.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) This continued an impressive turn through the Dbacks starting rotation as they group has allowed a grand total of 5 ER over their last 5 starts. Bratt continued to demonstrate poise and presence beyond his years tonight as he navigated his way through the Rockies lineup while striking out 4 Rockies batters. However as mentioned earlier, it was really the offense that let the Dbacks down again tonight in what has become a trend of scoring early and then getting shut down. It is worth noting that Sugano has had quite a bit of success against the Dbacks this season as he has allowed just 6 ER across just over 17 innings of work.

slides.title: SF Giants ride quality pitching, Bryce Eldridge homer to 4-1 victory over Astros
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>Winning a close game where the Giants ran the bases opportunistically and the other team committed a bunch of errors? That’s some weird, wild stuff. Carson Whisenhunt had a rough start, letting six of the first nine Astros he faced reach base. But he escaped and eventually earned his third win of the season after giving up just one run in 5.2 innings. Then Carson Seymour came through with two shutout innings of relief, yielding only a single to “Late Night” LaMonte Wade, Jr.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) It was a different sort of game for the Giants, who continued their hard-luck ways Monday when Andrew Susac fouled a ball off leg and fractured his kneecap, which will keep him off the field and off his scooter for the foreseeable future. But Tuesday, the breaks started to go their way. In the first inning, Whisenhunt escaped a bases-loaded jam, caused by a walk, a single and hitting Jose Altuve with a pitch.

slides.title: Royals game goes to extra innings and you already know how that story ends
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>Royals starter Michael Wacha pitched well into the seventh inning and the offense rallied in the eighth inning, but the bullpen did what it does best—give up runs and lose baseball games. Most of this game was rather uneventful because Wacha and Blake Snell were cruising for most of it. Mookie Betts smacked a solo home run in the second inning and Salvador Perez lifted a sacrifice fly in the fourth inning, but most of the action happened in the final four frames.

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) In the seventh inning, Alex Call doubled home Mookie Betts to give the Dodgers the lead, and then Teoscar Hernandez doubled to score Call and push the lead to two. Alex for the lead! pic. twitter. com/4NjhGQO9P3— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) August 12, 2026Kansas City battled back the very next frame.

slides.title: Blake Snell has a stellar start and Dodgers get walk-off win over Royals
slides.body: <<<INDENT>>>Blake Snell pitches during the fourth inning Tuesday. (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times)Dodgers southpaw Blake Snell called his shot. It wasn’t quite Babe Ruth pointing from the batter’s box. The moment won’t make its way into any movie. But Snell did tell manager Dave Roberts over text message that he was going to throw six innings in his first start back from the injured list after undergoing surgery to remove loose bodies from his elbow. Then, en route to a 5-4 walk-

<<<INDENT>>>(cont) off Dodgers victory in 10 innings against the Royals, Snell did just that. “I knew that’s what the plan was coming in, and I really wanted to execute that plan,” Snell said after limiting the Royals to one run and three hits. Despite Snell’s resume, the two-time Cy Young winner wasn’t guaranteed a smooth return. It had been three months since he’d last started a major-league game.
